eyebrow: Whole organization · unrestricted gift · US mailing access
program: Conditional value of an ordinary $100,000 NEXT gift

nutshell.headline: Mailing can close naloxone access gaps, but NEXT's marginal cost and future use remain unmeasured.
nutshell.body: Central whole-gift donor cost is $172,973 per10 US QALYs and $8,648,649 per10 Bay QALYs; SF has no priced positive health under the current mailing exclusion. This is a prior-based partial-health estimate, not a verified marginal offer.
nutshell.whyItMayWork: A current online/affiliate delivery network reaches people who report difficulty using existing routes. A supplied course may change whether a future overdose is fatal.
nutshell.whyWeAreCautious: Delivery counts are not unique deaths prevented. Public funding, partner costs, alternative rescue and repeated recipients materially dilute attribution.
nutshell.recommendationBlocker: No current costed next-gift package, unique-beneficiary denominator or incremental first-use outcome cohort. Favorable joint scenarios are not a probability-weighted recommendation.

summary.label: Central donor /10 QALYs
summary.detail: Same full $100,000 numerator, nested health shares; no population allocation.

summary.label: Central allocation
summary.detail: Whole-gift marginal prior; includes attributable overhead, not audited allocation.

summary.label: Resources
summary.detail: Explicit medicine/partner/medical priors; no resource savings centrally.

summary.label: Current funding room
summary.detail: FY2025 deficit is historical; public grants and an appeal do not establish an open marginal package.

programSection.body: NEXT operates an online and mail-based harm-reduction platform with over30 partners. Affiliates can supply medicine and fulfill orders; donations to NEXT are not donations to every partner. Other supplies, education and support remain inside the gift cost but their health is unquantified.

steps.title: Allocate the whole gift
steps.detail: $50,000 supports naloxone courses including attributable staff/platform overhead; remaining $50,000 retains its cost.

steps.title: Deduplicate additional access
steps.detail: 500 nominal courses become 250 added courses and125 distinct at-risk beneficiaries after separate financing and overlap priors.

steps.title: Model a first eligible use
steps.detail: A finite one-year opportunity window and competing mortality yield21.91 expected unique first events. Never one saved life per spray, kit or report.

steps.title: Value finite additional survival
steps.detail: Compare signed conditional death risk at the first event against existing care, then follow only that person's finite survival difference.

programSection.boundary: No assumed SF mail service, unlimited refills, extra lifetimes from repeated rescues, or sums with HRT/Remedy benefits for the same supply chain.

model.headline: One indexed rescue episode per distinct beneficiary; finite future health
model.body: All causal quantities are priors. US central 5.78125 QALYs includes no infection, morbidity, social-support or spillover benefits. Ordinary gifts do not inherit an all-naloxone allocation.

equation.label: First-event survival bridge
equation.expression: C = gift × allocation / course cash; N = C × funding additionality × distinct-beneficiary fraction. Qbenefit = N × signed conditional fatality difference × utility × exp(−discount×delay) × ∫[0,min(access,horizon)] event_hazard × exp[−(event_hazard+mortality+discount)t] × annuity(mortality+discount,horizon−t) dt. Qnet subtracts per-added-course and independent gift-date losses, including displaced alternative health.
equation.result: 5.78124985 US /0.115625 Bay /0 SF QALYs. Central US donor/gross/net costs $172,973 /$215,147 /$194,060 per10 QALYs.

inputs.label: Whole unrestricted gift
inputs.basis: Full gift remains numerator in all scenarios.

inputs.label: Naloxone allocation
inputs.basis: Marginal prior including attributable central overhead; other 50% health unquantified, cost retained.

inputs.label: NEXT cash per complete supported course
inputs.basis: Unpriced prior covering platform, staff, postage, recruitment failures and attributable administration. Not sprays, old cost/volume division or outside partner resources.

inputs.label: Funding additionality
inputs.basis: Fraction of courses added beyond public/other donor funding. Not clinical efficacy or allocation.

inputs.label: Distinct at-risk beneficiaries per added course
inputs.basis: Deduplicates repeat orders, shared responders and overlapping programs. At most one lifetime stream/person; secondary population multipliers excluded.

inputs.label: First eligible use hazard
inputs.basis: First adequate-course rescue opportunity, not all overdoses or reported reversals/mailed kits.

inputs.label: Finite access window
inputs.basis: No credited new use after access ends; excludes subsequent repeat-use benefit.

inputs.label: Finite health horizon from activation
inputs.basis: Same finite end date for early and late index rescues.

inputs.label: Implementation delay
inputs.basis: Health discounted from activation to gift date; population defined at activation.

inputs.label: Common competing/future mortality
inputs.basis: Explicit prior includes non-index overdoses before first event and all future mortality after it; prevents a permanent saved-life assumption.

inputs.label: Continuous health discount
inputs.basis: Judgment; not 3% effective annual compounding.

inputs.label: Survivor utility
inputs.basis: Not healthy life expectancy or directly measured NEXT utility.

inputs.label: Conditional death-risk reduction
inputs.basis: Signed difference relative to actual alternative rescue/EMS, including adequate supply and readiness. Not a drug success rate.

inputs.label: Burden per added course
inputs.basis: Applies to all added courses, including those without a credited unique beneficiary. Excludes any harm already in fatality difference.

inputs.label: Independent harm
inputs.basis: Survives zero allocation. No second discount.

inputs.label: Displaced alternative health
inputs.basis: Distinct crowd-out of other medicine/partner uses, beyond replacement courses already removed. Not a counterfactual assumption of no public care.

inputs.label: Outside public resources
inputs.basis: Real medicine/partner inputs excluding expenses paid by NEXT or subcontract invoices already counted. Public transfers themselves are not extra resource costs.

inputs.label: Outside private/volunteer resources
inputs.basis: Real inputs outside NEXT cash; excludes upstream/downstream duplicate payment.

inputs.label: Additional medical resources per eligible event
inputs.basis: Expected incremental real EMS/aftercare, not a billed reimbursement or a claim every event causes a new ambulance trip.

inputs.label: Other net real resource savings
inputs.basis: Separate unmeasured public/private resource savings, not transfers. Negative input denotes extra costs. Not a benefit estimate.

inputs.label: Benefit in nine-county Bay Area
inputs.basis: Independent residence prior outside SF, not population share or California statewide delivery share.

inputs.label: Benefit in SF
inputs.basis: Official mail exclusion. Mobility/secondary rescue spillovers not established.

inputs.label: Loss in Bay Area
inputs.basis: Separate residence share of course harms, independent harms and displaced alternative health; no addition to US total.

inputs.label: Loss in SF
inputs.basis: Not mechanically constrained to match benefit share; default no SF effect.

model.uncertaintyBoundary: These are judgmental scenarios, not confidence bounds. Favorable US $3,760/10 requires joint optimistic allocation, cost, additionality, uniqueness, use, efficacy and survival. The central value does not meet $100,000/10. Null and negative effects retain costs. Shorter access and survival matter. Public-resource savings can create a negative net-resource price without changing health; this is a diagnostic, not claimed savings.
model.fundingBoundary: FY2025 Form990 shows $738,924 government grants and $426,200 deficit, but no priced current incremental course offer. Gross resources use all nominal courses; net outside inputs use only financing-additional courses, plus expected incremental medical resources, less explicitly specified real savings. Neither is gross organization revenue, billed insurance, or a public transfer sum.

evidence.result: Functioning multi-state network; Oregon partner reports2,342 mail recipients in2024.
evidence.transfer: One affiliate count is not a network denominator, marginal reach or complete unit cost.

evidence.population: Early NEXT recipients and voluntarily reported rescues
evidence.transfer: No extraction of a current use probability or unique deaths prevented; repeat and voluntary reports are not causal health.

evidence.result: Naloxone reverses respiratory depression; repeat doses and emergency care may be needed.
evidence.transfer: Does not supply the marginal death-risk difference versus actual alternative rescue.
No current course denominator, marginal allocation or verified funding room.

reservations: All unit costs, causal probabilities and residence shares except the SF delivery boundary remain uncalibrated judgments.
A complete course can require multiple doses; future use is not inferred from reports divided by doses.
Finite mortality includes future overdose attrition, but recipient-specific risk and mobility are unknown.
Outside resources exclude amounts already paid through NEXT contracts. Verify this cost ledger before using the result for a donation.
Do not add health from NEXT, HRT, Remedy or local affiliate models without removing same-medicine and same-person overlap.
excludedBenefits: HIV/HCV and other infection prevention from sterile supplies
Education, stigma reduction and social support beyond the first modeled rescue
Additional secondary beneficiaries or repeat rescue episodes
